turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You entered a zero on Owen's essay without calling me, and he found out on his phone in the middle of class. I have a call at 4:40, Hale. Who decided on that zero, and on what basis?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing that down: 11:31, 11:52, 11:58. Kids draft somewhere else and paste it in, Hale. Who else has seen this?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine, Hale. Whatever happens with this essay, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. Is there anything on his file right now?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line is a bad citation, Hale, not proof of anything. I'm searching it myself. And you still haven't told me what's on his file.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I've searched it, Hale. Okay. What's on his file right now, and what exactly are you proposing?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.

Forty minutes in class against a take-home essay is not a fair comparison, Hale, and you know it. That's three things you've shown me and not one answer to my two questions. His file, and your proposal.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, and to put this behind him, Owen will do the rewrite. Tonight's email says it's private, its mark replaces the zero, nothing is on his file now or later, and it's marked before December 1. And the zero comes out of the gradebook until then, Hale.
Will he do it?
He'll do it, Hale. Put the date and the room in that email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Today you agreed under procedure 4.4 that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite, not in front of his class, whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record. I still require that the zero come out of the gradebook until then, that the rewrite be marked before December 1, that you confirm nothing is on his file now, and that you give me the date and the room. I expect that in writing tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite to put this behind him; she still wants the zero out of the gradebook in the meantime, the rewrite marked before December 1, written confirmation that nothing is on his file now, and a date and room; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then answered her paste-it-in defence by inviting her to bring the other file's dates, because it was specific, dated, his own work, and something she could check.
What cost ground: You went several turns without answering her direct question about what was on his file, which kept her guarded and made her repeat her demand.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's writing in the late hours of a night in October, right on top of what she had refused to think about, which is why she went short and hard there; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on his file, right after the version history, answer it plainly in one sentence before showing your next document.
